profile.campus: True North Data campus, Loudoun County, VA (Loudoun County zoning case ZMAP-2017-0003, PIN 194103673000, approved Jan 2018)
profile.reading: This building sits at 42254 Thunderball Drive in Leesburg, Virginia, part of a data center campus that Loudoun County own zoning and permitting records identify by the project name True North Data. Loudoun County zoning case ZMAP-2017-0003, filed under that project name, rezoned roughly 105 acres to Planned Development-Office Park specifically to allow data center uses, and was approved January 18, 2018. The underlying parcel, county PIN 194103673000, covering roughly 97 acres, is recorded under a condominium-regime plat named True North Land Condo, a legal structure commonly used to subdivide one large hyperscale campus parcel into separately titled buildings, consistent with the six separate addresses and building records that make up this cluster. A 2019 grading permit for a project called True North 2 described three data center buildings with utilities, and a 2023 stormwater permit for True North Data Phase 2A covered a further 16.5 acres of disturbed area, indicating a phased expansion. Four tenant fit-up zoning permits were issued across April and May 2025, suggesting the campus was still being built out in phases as recently as that year. No document reviewed this session, however, gives a total megawatt capacity, final building count, or total square footage for the completed campus, and the identity of the corporate entity that actually filed the original 2017 rezoning application is not exposed in the county public zoning-case layer, so True North Data Solutions, the name this record carries as operator, could not be independently confirmed as a registered company through the Virginia State Corporation Commission this session. Loudoun County is widely described as the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and Leesburg location within it, near the eastern edge of the county fiber and power-dense corridor, is consistent with why a developer would pursue a multi-building campus of this scale here specifically.

sources.title: True North Data Solutions — corporate site

profile.research_note: True North Data Solutions' own site publishes only company-wide totals ("10+ project sites," "673 MW capacity & growing" across 3 countries) with no facility-specific pages or addresses -- corporate office listed is in Calgary, AB. This Leesburg/Loudoun County VA campus (off Thunderball Drive) is reported in local press as a build-to-suit project (Compass Datacenters broke ground for True North); no public per-building spec sheet exists. One row on file is separately named "TikTok Data Center," consistent with reporting that this campus is a single-tenant build-to-suit, which explains the absence of public marketing specs.

reading.body:
The True North Data campus in Leesburg occupies approximately 97 acres rezoned in January 2018 specifically for data center use, with a legal structure and phased permitting pattern consistent with a hyperscale multi-building development. Four tenant fit-up permits issued in April and May 2025 indicate construction was ongoing as recently as that year, and a 2023 stormwater permit covered a 16.5-acre expansion phase. The campus capacity in megawatts is not published, making its scale within Virginia unknowable from operator disclosure.

Virginia has 330 mapped data center facilities, of which only 23 publish capacity figures totaling 1,375 MW. This Leesburg campus ranks 24th among Virginia facilities with published capacity, meaning it either publishes no figure or publishes a figure smaller than all 23 published capacities in the state. The operator, True North Data Solutions, publishes only a company-wide total of 673 MW across 10 or more project sites in three countries, with no per-facility breakdown.

Leesburg sits in Loudoun County, widely described as the largest data center market in the world by capacity, and the True North campus location near the county's eastern fiber and power corridor is consistent with why developers pursue multi-building campuses of this scale there. The absence of public per-building specifications and reports that the campus is a single-tenant build-to-suit project mean the campus capacity and operating status remain opaque to public assessment.
